title: Vegan Cottage Pie
subtitle: Mushroom and lentil filling with a smooth mashed potato top, fully plant-based
excerpt: Vegan cottage pie builds its filling from brown lentils and finely chopped mushrooms in a rich, dark gravy. The mash on top uses olive oil instead of butter. The result has the same stick-to-your-ribs quality as the original, with none of the blandness that sometimes dogs vegan cooking when the seasoning is not pushed far enough.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze assembled and unbaked for up to 3 months. Defrost overnight, then bake at 180°C fan for 40 minutes from cold.
recipe.batchNotes: Ideal for batch cooking. The flavour improves the next day.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make the filling up to 3 days ahead. Top and bake on the day.

content.text: Vegan cottage pie needs bold seasoning to match the depth that beef mince and stock bring naturally to the original. Marmite, tomato puree, and soy sauce together build an umami layer that the lentils and mushrooms absorb during the long braise. Do not be tempted to shorten the simmering time: the filling needs to reduce until it is almost dry, then the stock is added and it reduces again.

items.prepNote: finely chopped to a mince-like texture

content.text: Heat a drizzle of oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Cook {{chestnut-mushrooms}} of finely chopped mushrooms until all their liquid has evaporated and they are beginning to colour, about 10 minutes. Do not stir too often. Set aside on a plate.

In the same pan, cook {{onion}} chopped onion, {{carrot}} diced carrot, and {{celery}} diced celery in a little oil for 10 minutes until soft. Add {{garlic}} of crushed garlic and the thyme. Cook for 1 minute. Stir in {{tomato-puree}} of tomato puree and cook for 2 minutes. Return the mushrooms to the pan.

Add {{brown-lentils}} of rinsed lentils, {{marmite}} of Marmite, {{worcestershire-sauce}} of Worcestershire sauce, and {{stock-vegetable}} of stock. Add the bay leaves. Simmer uncovered for 30 to 35 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the lentils are tender and the gravy is thick. Remove the bay leaves. Season well.

Boil {{potato}} of potato chunks in salted water until tender, about 18 minutes. Drain and steam dry. Mash with {{olive-oil}} of olive oil and enough hot water to reach a smooth, spreadable consistency. Season well.
Heat the oven to 200°C fan. Spoon the filling into a baking dish. Spread the mash on top and fork into ridges. Bake for 25 to 30 minutes until the top is golden in places and the edges are bubbling.

items.cause: Insufficient umami , the Marmite and tomato puree are doing the work that beef does in the original.
items.fix: Increase the Marmite to 2 teaspoons and the tomato puree to 4 tablespoons. Taste at the end and add a little soy sauce if it still needs depth.

items.symptom: The mushrooms have gone watery into the filling
items.cause: They were not dried out fully before being added.
items.fix: Cook the mushrooms alone over high heat until all moisture has evaporated and they are starting to brown. Only then add them back.

items.symptom: The olive oil mash is greasy
items.cause: Too much oil was added all at once while the potatoes were too warm.
items.fix: Mash the potato, let it cool for 2 minutes, then fold in the olive oil gradually. The mash should be creamy, not oily.

items.symptom: The filling is too loose under the mash
items.cause: The stock did not reduce sufficiently before baking.
items.fix: Simmer until you can drag a spoon across the surface and no liquid fills the gap. The filling firms as it cools slightly before the mash goes on.

content.text: Vegan cottage pie became a fixture of British plant-based cooking because lentils and mushrooms can carry the weight of a mince-based braise. The form works. The ingredients work. It is one of the best vegan takes on a British classic, and it tastes like a dish in its own right, not a workaround.
